I wound up popping an AMD Instinct MI210 (64GB HBM2, 1600GB/s) into my existing main Proxmox node, and passing it through to a VM.

So it is less of an “AI rig” and more of a large hypervisor that also has a VM that does AI stuff, as one of its uses.

image1024×768 174 KB

image1920×1446 596 KB

Turns out that despite having a proper server with good airflow front to back, that just wasn’t sufficient for cooling the thing.

I tried one of these 3d printed 80mm fan shrouds I found on eBay, but it was too large and didn’t fit:

image1920×1446 517 KB

So I wound up ghetto modding it by cutting up a plastic cutting board and making my own shroud and using foil tape to hold it together.

It looks a little ghetto, but it gets the job done.

Hey, I’m thoroughly jealous of the MI210. That’s a lot of GB/s

It is, and it comes in handy sometimes (2500 tokens/s pre-fill and 80 tokens/s eval on Gemma4:26b) but it is a little bit more impressive on paper than it is in reality (something I didn’t realize until after I bought it)

It turns out AMD’s ecosystem is nowhere near as optimized as Nvidia’s, so when it comes to efficiency, I rarely get more than 60% of the theoretical max throughput, which is a bit of a bummer. But it is still quite nice.

I did also realize after the fact that this earlier generation of Instinct cards lacks FP8 support which also stings a little…

I do really appreciate the high speed pre-fills though (though I admit, I don’t fully know how that compares to other hardware out there)

A ~30b class dense model at Q8_0 usually evaluates at about 25-30 tokens/s, which is less exciting than I had hoped for when I forked over the cash for the thing, but that’s what happens when you first get into stuff. You learn along the way, make mistakes, and some of them are expensive.

If I had to make a decision all over again, for the money I spent, I might get a couple of DGX sparks. They would evaluate much slower due to their much lower memory bandwidth, but damn would it be nice to have 256GB of RAM.

It’s just the cost of learning

I appreciate the info, but yeah, the figures I am seeing are with llama.cpp compiled with HIP support and all of the special gfx90a flags in it (which was a pain in the ass due to all of the dependency conflicts)

I tried a few different versions of ROCm (my theory was that more recent ones might be more optimized for more recent GPU’s and older ones might be better, but that turned out to have negligible effect)

At least it did better this way in llama.cpp than in vLLM, which I never got working satisfactorily due to performance kernels in it not supporting the gfx90a architecture.

But the AMD ROCm drivers just suck. I’ve had one too many mornings where I’d come down and the displays had crashed (Linux, Gentoo, XLibre) and the kernel logs would be filled with AMD errors. Sometimes I’d just be crashed out to the login screen and would have to load everything back up. It has 96GB of RAM (scavenged from other machines that now have SODIMM/Laptop ram with adapters) and a a dedicated 512GB nvme drive for swap and I still run into issues.

So I decided to get some other crap for AI workflows:

image1920×1440 541 KB

On the floor is a 2019 Mac Pro with 96GB of DDR4 and 1TB of storage I got off eBay for $2066 (including shipping and taxes). I got Gentoo on it with ZFS encryption (blog post coming soon on it) and got the LLMs to write some scripts so the fans properly cool the MPX video card it came with (AMD 5xxx something .. 16GB of ram .. slow).

I also got that pre-built with a 5090. It was ~$7k and I wouldn’t have considered it if it wasn’t for the fact that 5090s jumped to $8k! Integrators still had some of the previous stock, and getting a 5090 with 32GB RAM and 2TB of storage for that price seemed like “If I don’t do it now, I won’t be able to in a month” … and now I look at Newegg and all of the 5090 prebuilts are at $10k!

The 5090 struggles due to the 32GB of ram, so I’ll probably shuffle some sticks out of the old rig. I originally though about adding an external power supply to the Mac and dropping the 5090 in there, but the Mac only supports 12 inch cards and the 5090 is … way longer. I’m not going to rig up some crazy risers or anything, so the Mac will likely get the R9700 and a 3080-Ti when I get all the power cables I ordered. It’s got over 1000w power supply so I think it can handle those.

The 16GB card it came with will probably go to LLMs/Ollama and the other two for Image/Video work.
